notes.title: Consistent Story, Consistent Art
notes.content:
[p]Hi everyone![/p][p]Today’s update is a big one — not just in size, but in importance. In previous updates, I’ve explained how the game delivers a cohesive and immersive story, regardless of how unusual or unique your character choices are. Continuing along that path, I’m excited to announce a brand-new, fully handcrafted art style for the Spirit![/p][p]Let me take you behind the scenes a bit.[/p][p]From the very beginning, I dreamed of [i]Guiding Spirit[/i] having handcrafted visuals — something that would give it the feeling of a beautifully illustrated storybook. One of my biggest inspirations was the [i]Sword & Sorcery[/i] gamebooks. I remember getting lost in those pages, just staring at the art long after I'd read the text.[/p][p]When I began working on the [i]Guiding Spirit[/i], I knew the game’s concept. But the visuals? Not so much. For the earliest builds, I used pencil sketches and free asset packs — and honestly, the result wasn’t great. I had little experience with digital art, and no tools to support it.[/p][p]I considered simplifying trait icons, but many of the Spirit’s traits — like [i]Awkward[/i], [i]Complainer[/i], or [i]Trustworthy[/i] — are hard to express through minimalistic symbols. During early playtests, testers struggled to tell them apart. It became clear: I needed something more expressive or I need to scrap the concept of trait icons overall and just use text to list traits for the player.[/p][p]I also experimented with removing character portraits, but that just added more confusion again. Without a visual identity, testers couldn’t quickly recognize the misfit band they had assembled — which often led to frustration. They’d start a story, read paragraphs of text, only to realize they actually intended to create a different team.[/p][p]And last but not the least: story illustrations. I’ve always wanted the game to [i]feel[/i] like a book — not just through the writing, but visually. I knew I had to be careful, though, since the game relies heavily on imagination, and with the many possible story permutations, the illustrations couldn’t be too specific.[/p][p]Because of all the above, I began searching for an artist to help bring those key moments to life. I reached out to numerous of them— each responded with kindness and professionalism. However, most were already booked for several months, and based on their feedback, producing the artwork needed for the demo alone would take at least a year. And we are only speaking about the story illustrations, excluding portraits or icons! It is completely understandable, of course—doing art the right way is a full-time commitment, and they had other projects on their plates.[/p][p]With the game nearing feature-complete, I didn’t want to delay the entire project for another 2–3 years just for visuals. Furthermore, I wanted to announce the game so I could begin networking and establishing social media channels in preparation for the upcoming demo. One could say that I started looking for an artist too late and should have done so earlier, which is technically true. However, part of the reason is that I didn’t settle on the final concept of the Spirit until early last year (the project took many different forms over the last 6 years), and it was only then that I began to understand in what format the game could present it's content to the player.[/p][p]In a moment of desperation, I began experimenting with AI-generated art to create a trailer and replace most of the old in-game assets. It helped me get the word out and made the game “presentable” — but unfortunately the visuals became a chaotic mix of AI images and mismatched free to use assets.[/p][p]The feedback I received: while the premise of [i]Guiding Spirit[/i] feels unique and interesting, the inconsistent art style brakes immersion. Someone said, [i]“I’d rather play an ugly but consistent game than a shiny mess.”[/i] And honestly? I felt the same way. This just didn’t feel right.[/p][p]Additionally, the AI-generated images often lacked consistency, making it difficult to convey a clear, unique vision. I began to realize that some of the originality was being lost, as I had to make compromises—especially when it came to depicting exotic species or specific items I came up with. I kept running into all sorts of issues and felt like I didn’t have the control I needed. Maybe I was just bad at managing it—but in the end, that doesn’t really matter, and here’s why.[/p][p]Shortly after the announcement, I was able to get my hands on a drawing tablet and i started to sketch. I began watching digital art tutorials online and experimented with different art styles. Eventually, I came across a particular line art style that was simple enough to handle for everything, yet detailed enough to add depth and multiple layers to the experience.[/p][p]Eliminating color might not be everyone's favorite choice, but I did it for two key reasons: First, testers frequently mentioned that it breaks immersion when portraits don’t exactly match the colors they picked during character creation—a challenge that also extends to NPCs and location artwork. By switching everything to black and white, I can lean on the player’s imagination and cover a broader range of visual possibilities. Second, as a solo developer, spending time coloring every piece would significantly slow down progress on other crucial aspects of the game.[/p][p]Working on the in-game assets reminded me once again how incredible the creative process feels. Even though I knew it would be a lot of work, I started to feel optimistic and genuinely enjoyed having full control over my creations. Once I had something halfway decent, I implemented it in the game and I showed it to testers — and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. The line art, hand-drawn style fits the storybook UI perfectly. It blends naturally with the text, and it’s something I can realistically complete without holding up the development of other game features.[/p][p]One by one, I replaced [i]every[/i] asset: icons, portraits, buttons, filters, story illustrations. And now, I’m thrilled (and honestly, a little relieved) to say: Everything in the game is handcrafted now. I also updated the trailer and promotional materials accordingly. Even the book background and paper tooltips have been replaced. 

For full transparency, I drew inspiration from the AI images I already had—much like researching online or reading books—especially when I really liked the characters’ poses or the scene’s composition. I used them as a supplementary tool rather than a definitive solution. Ultimately, I’m now able to take creative liberties in how I portray the characters and present their traits, which is the main purpose of doing this myself.[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45618951/f0b9a29a9df432825debcb4e46a8360b7c293f51.jpg"][/img][/p][p]There’s still a lot of work ahead for future chapters, but I’ve found the right approach to handle it. Illustrator [b]Krisztina Boros[/b] is also helping me by creating beautiful art for the in-game lorebooks. You’ll be able to browse these books during your adventure like little collectible stories. She’s amazingly gifted — I’m excited to show you some of her work soon!

Also huge thanks to [url="https://x.com/Alderdoodle"]@Alderdoodle[/url] for her beautiful borders, title frames and page dividers![/p][p]The game now has a [b]consistent visual style[/b] that complements the tone and world of [i]Guiding Spirit[/i]. I know it may not appeal to everyone, but im pretty satisfied with it (it still needs some polish), i think it blends into the book interface very well. Also it feels [i]mine.[/i][/p][p]Over the last few months, when I wasn’t drawing, I was writing and coding — and in the [i]next update[/i], I’ll be sharing details about the upcoming [b]free demo[/b]![/p][p]I also had a fantastic time chatting with the great @remulto4 on his DEV.LIFE show, you can watch the episode here:[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=87TE2reQLOU"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]Thank you all so much for your support, feedback, and patience. It’s helping shape this project in the best way possible.[/p][p]Until next time,
[b]Dice Impact[/b][/p]

notes.title: What are you capable of?
notes.content:
[p]Greetings, Spirits![/p][p]I hope you're staying cool out there—because here the sun is blazing, the AC is barely holding on, and my keyboard is in danger of melting. Still, despite the heat wave, here’s a cool new update to share with you.[/p][p]Today I’m talking about Capability Traits![/p][p][/p][h3]What are you capable of?[/h3][p]In [i]The Guiding Spirit[/i], you can choose from [b]over 70 unique capability traits[/b] to customize your character’s strengths, style, and identity, a set of attributes that directly influence how they survive, adapt, and endure in a world woven with mystery and danger.[/p][p]These traits either [b]help[/b] or [b]hinder[/b] the journey, depending on whether they are Standard or Challenging. Challenging Traits introduce obstacles that make survival harder, but also unlock deeper story moments, more rewarding triumphs, and unique paths that only those who dare to struggle will see.[/p][p]Will your character be nimble but sickly? Sharp of mind, but haunted by fear? These are the stories that make legends.  Certain traits may unlock others—while some may lock you out of conflicting ones. [i]Choose "Clumsy"? You won’t be able to take "Agile."  [/i]Your choices define not only the characters' strengths but the weaknesses they must learn to survive with—or overcome. 

See below some examples:[/p][p][b]Tall[/b]: His height gave him not only power but perspective—a vantage point that let him see over walls, through enemy lines, and anticipate moves before they unfolded.

[b]Lightweight[/b]: Enemies who underestimated Elenni’s size quickly learned that lightness could be lethal.

[b]One eye[/b] (Challenging): Varek’s weathered face was marked by countless scars—but none more striking than the empty socket covered by a leather patch, worn and stitched with care.[/p][p][b]Strong[/b]: Tharn lifted the pillar with brute force[/p][p][b]Endurance[/b]: Sasha had been running since dawn—over ridges, through ravines, across shallow streams and sun-scorched plains.

[b]Shaky hands[/b] (Challenging): For the Intellect Elowen whose power depended on precise gestures and unwavering focus, this trembling was both a curse and a challenge.[/p][p][b]Quick-thinker[/b]: Tara’s golden eyes were scanning, calculating.

[b]Mnemonist[/b]: Adyr’s mind was a vault, a labyrinth of memory stretching back over 500 years.[/p][p][b]Multitasker[/b] : To Sylren, chaos was not confusion. It was opportunity.[/p][p][b]Adrenaline addict[/b] (Challenging): Vex lived for the heartbeat before the storm—the electrifying moment when danger loomed and the world narrowed to sharp focus.[/p][p][b]Imbecile[/b] (Challenging): Gorb always struggled to make sense of even the simplest instructions. He once tried to “help” a wizard by tossing what he thought was a healing potion into a fire, causing an unexpected explosion that destroyed half the tavern.[/p][p][b]Claustrophobic[/b]: Helmets, in particular, were Liora’s nightmare. The moment one touched her scalp, her breath would quicken, her vision would blur, and panic would claw at her chest like a trapped beast.[/p][p][b]Strong immune[/b]: Nyra trudged through the festering swamp without a mask.[/p][p][b]Eagle eye[/b]: Kaelen could spot an ambush long before it struck.[/p][p][b]Smeller[/b]: While others relied on sight or sound, Liora trusted the invisible trails carried on the wind—the faintest trace of smoke, the subtle scent of crushed pine needles, the lingering musk of a hidden foe.[/p][p][b]Domain magic[/b]: Each spell Seraphina cast was a thread woven directly from Alondra’s divine power, a spark of dark fire igniting despair in the heart of enemies.[/p][p][b]Scales[/b]:[b] [/b]Draven’s skin was covered in tough, emerald-green lizard scales that shimmered like polished armor beneath the sunlight.[/p][p][b]Fear of spiders[/b] (Challenging): Even the smallest spider sent a shiver down Kaela’s spine and tightened her breath.[/p][p][b]Rich start[/b]: Rynn’s fingers danced over the coins as he thought, “At last… fortune favors the bold.”[/p][p][b]Tough start[/b] (Challenging): Mira was lucky to walk away with only a few bruises and a busted lip.[/p][p][b]Undead [/b](Challenging): Alaric was no longer truly alive, yet not entirely dead—a revenant caught between worlds, bound to walk again.[/p][p]And there’s much more - but I don’t want to spill everything just yet. :)[/p][p][/p][h3]The Weight of the Road[/h3][p]While each party member begins the journey with their own unique [b]abilities and disabilities[/b], their state of mind and body will continue to change as the adventure unfolds.[/p][p]As they travel through the wild forests and treacherous mountains of Anderelm, they'll gain [b]further traits[/b] that reflect the toll of the journey. They might get tired, hungry, thirsty, or just fed up with the monotony of the road.   These traits affect how characters behave, interact, and perform. A tired warrior might swing more slowly. A hungry rogue might snap at companions. But with care, rest, and good leadership, these temporary traits can be managed—or even turned into moments of growth.[/p][p][/p][h3]Inspirations behind The Spirit[/h3][p]Beyond talking about Character Creation, I wanted to pull back the curtain and talk about the titles that helped shape my vision. To dive deeper into those influences, I’ve recently released a short video on the Spirit YouTube channel where I reflect in more detail on how these games’ve helped me bring this project to life:[/p][previewyoutube="WEOV2LiQuEY;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]That’s all for this update![/p][p]As always, thank you for being part of the journey. Whether you're wishlisting the game, follow us on any of our social media channels, or just cheering us on, your support means the world to us. More updates are coming, there’s a lot more to talk about, so stay tuned—and stay cool out there (especially if your weather is anything like ours).[/p][p]Until next time,
Dice Impact[/p]

notes.title: Creating Memorable, Complex Characters
notes.content:
[p]Hello everyone,

I want to start by saying: [b]You are incredible![/b] [/p][p]All the incoming wishlists help me to complete the game I’ve always wanted to make and I believe together we can create something very unique.[/p][p]I couldn’t contain my excitement so here’s the second update and it’s about...[/p][p](drum roll)[/p][p]...character creation and how to craft a unique backstory![/p][p][/p][h3]The Bard Who Chased Danger[/h3][p]Let’s take a look at an example of a distinctive origin tale you can create in the game.[/p][p]Let’s say you pick the Scurg ancestry for your character. These are adrenaline-addict creatures, always looking for danger, tough situations keep them alive.  For Class, you choose the bard. Because bards are cool. In the world of The Guiding Spirit, bards do not neccesarily have access to the Intellect (magic), they might simply be a chanter making a living in shady taverns or a jester hired by the Wind-King to entertain his royal court. How they became a bard? That depends entirely on their [b]Origin Story[/b].  

Speaking of! For Origin, you pick „Merchant family”, but let’s say that when you distribute your skill-points you don’t put any points in Trade. So how that is presented in their backstory? Well, your character was raised by merchants but every time their father counted his profit, their mind was elsewhere. Where exactly? If you did put points in Arcane skills, the story will call out that instead of learning the basic principles of trade, the character was secretly reading books about performing complex magical practises. If you designed the character to be a warrior, their story will mention that when nobody looked, they practised combat stances with a wooden sword (or any other weapon, depending on which weapon proficiency you selected!) in the backyard.
[i]
Will was born into a family of merchants, raised among ledgers and crates stacked high with goods from distant lands. His father expected him to follow in the family footsteps, mastering the art of trade and counting every coin with precision. Yet, every time his father sat down to tally profits, Will’s thoughts drifted far from the marketplace.[/i][/p][p][i]Instead of learning the basics of commerce, Will secretly slipped away to hidden corners of their home, where he pored over ancient books filled with complex magical practices. While others bargained and haggled, he studied spells and rituals—unlocking mysteries that promised power beyond mere wealth.[/i][/p][p][/p][h3]Every Trait Matters[/h3][p]From where do they get the equipment to do those things? It depends on what personality traits you gave to the character. A swindler might “borrow” those books and training materials with practiced subtlety. A more aggressive—or perhaps downright cruel—character could simply intimidate someone into handing them over. But a clever, quick-thinking individual? They’ll find a way no one sees coming.[/p][p]But let’s keep this simple for now, you can go crazy when you'll try out the demo (coming later this year for free!). Your scurg character never wanted to be a merchant, they took their father’s old, never-before-used lute and went to seek adventure and danger (mind, you are a scurg, you need danger!). You pick the „Rich Start” and „Missing Finger” capability traits, among others. But wait... you didn’t pick the „Noble Kid” Origin, so how Rich Start is going to work? [/p][p]Let’s see what has been added to their backstory:   [/p][p][i]She was even lucky enough to stumble upon a small fortune on her first day of travel—pure chance. Unfortunately, the bandits who had hidden the chest tracked her down before sunset. She escaped with her life… though not without the cost of a finger.[/i][/p][p]Okay, that’s tense. But why exactly the character decided to become an adventurer, leaving behind their past? Maybe they have a more complex, specific reason? Lucky for you, you can define that as well! For simplicity, let’s choose the „Wants to be famous” Aspiration as it goes well with the bard class. If you mix that with the „Ambitious” personality trait, I promise you will get some very cool story-scenes! [/p][p]And there you go, you just created a unique, complex backstory with twists and turns.[/p][p][/p][h3]A memorable tale[/h3][p]And that’s not all—you can also customize your character’s core memories, followers, faith, constellation, specializations, special abilities (like spells and combat skills), and much more![/p][p]You change any aspect, you get a different concept. Find the one suitable for you and see how it plays out!  There are myriad of choices you can select from when it comes to Origins, Core Memories, Aspirations, Capabilities, Personality, Skills, Proficiencies, Followers and the unique combination of these will create memorable characters. Even if you pick the same Trait for two heroes in the party, every other aspect you selected for them will alter their background story enough to make them feel distinctive.

[i]It’s your world, your rules. You can create a character who works alone. You can create a character who doesn’t speak at all, not a word during the entire adventure. You can create a character who struggles to understand what others are saying. You can create a bard who is kicked-out of every tavern at their early days - and then witness exceptional character development - all because you forgot to put points into the Performance Skill (oops). The choice is yours.[/i]  

And keep in mind, your choices do not only change their backstory, they change the actual journey, they guide the story. Their aspirations, their past, their identity will decide what's happening to them, each npc will react to them based on who they are, what they do, in a nutshell: how you designed them. Also, it goes beyond the combination of an individual’s traits, the mixture of all your team members’ features will create unique outcomes, story beats. There are plenty of hidden storylines tucked away—only revealed when you use just the right combination of characters.

You can follow us for more updates wherever is most convenient for you:

[url="https://bsky.app/profile/theguidingspirit.bsky.social"]Bluesky[/url]

Until the next update,
Dice Impact[/p]

notes.title: The Guiding Spirit - Announcement Trailer
notes.content:
[h1]The adventure begins...[/h1][p]
Hey folks!

I'm very excited to announce The Guiding Spirit and put up its Steam page!
If you didn't see the announcement trailer, check it out below!
[/p][previewyoutube="GyZW3hqXc8A;full"][/previewyoutube][h2]Upcoming Demo[/h2][p]The game is feature-complete and im currently pouring more and more content into it. You will have the chance to try out the game yourself soon, as there will be a free demo, coming later this year. The content for the demo is already playable but I want it to be as polished as possible and completely (if such thing exists in the videogame industry) bug-free so you have the best possible experience when the time comes. 

[/p][h2]Updates[/h2][p]Over the next months, be on the lookout for regular updates on the game’s several features and behind-the-scenes looks at some of the creative processes going into The Guiding Spirit.
As an example, I plan to cover each aspect of Character Creation:
•	Ancestries
•	Deities
•	Constellations
•	Origins
•	Core Memories
•	Aspirations
•	Capabilities
•	Personality
•	Skills
•	Proficiencies
•	Special Abilities
•	Items
•	Followers

[/p][h2]Credit[/h2][p]Before i go I would like to credit the much-talented Misterbates (Kristof Rety) for the incredible music piece he created for the trailer (his channel can be found [url="https://www.youtube.com/@musicbymisterbates"]here[/url]). I’m going to share more of his work in the future, there are some very cool in-game soundtracks coming your way!

I’m also working with an illustrator for some special art to be added in the game, keep an eye out on the following updates for more info!

[/p][h2]Social Media[/h2][p]You can follow us wherever is most convenient for you:
[url="https://x.com/GuidingSpirit22"]X[/url]
[url="https://bsky.app/profile/theguidingspirit.bsky.social"]Bluesky[/url]

Until the next update,
[b]Dice Impact[/b][/p]
